article.name: deja-vu
article.summary: deja-vu is a local Go application that indexes existing coding-agent transcripts into a rebuildable inverted index and exposes search, context recall, handoff, and recovery through CLI/TUI, MCP, and hooks. It also supports explicit local notes and curated repository notes. This is a pinned source review; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The official README presents deja-vu as a local memory/search tool for coding-agent transcripts, with a Go binary, CLI/TUI, MCP server, plugins and lifecycle hooks. Its copyright line names Vladislav Shulcz; that attribution alone does not establish operational ownership or support commitments.

The official repository page identifies main as default. Its main Atom feed and full-SHA commit page identify 76aaac6b5e4c74d51916d604bbccaf34d50eb3de as the current head. Reviewed 2026-11-25T10:47:26Z (UTC; 2026-11-25 02:47:26 PST; America/Los_Angeles).

architecture.text: Source-specific parsers read supported harness transcript stores into a shared session/message model; file parsing can use a worker pool while index writes remain deterministically ordered. Inputs include JSONL, JSON and local SQLite stores, and indexing can work retroactively from transcripts already on disk.

The default derived index is under ~/.cache/deja/index.db and is organized as length-prefixed records, token posting buckets/overlays, session offsets and a manifest. Rebuilds track changed or replaced source sessions; dead records/postings are compacted or zeroed, making the index a derived cache rather than the canonical transcript store.

The indexed message model preserves roles including user, assistant, tool output, files, commands, edits and summaries. The architecture guide says non-speech roles can be filtered and are not ordinarily presented as user speech; explicit notes live in JSONL stores, while repository notes are stored separately in .deja/memory.jsonl.

behavior.text: Harnesses write their own transcripts; deja-vu parses and indexes them. The explicit `remember` command appends a tagged note locally or, with --repo, to curated repository memory. Its code checks write policy, masks detected secrets in notes, handles duplicate-note errors and refreshes the index unless manual indexing is configured.

Transcript rewrites are reflected in the derived index during indexing. The inspected `remember` path is append-oriented and does not establish an in-place edit/correction API for an existing local note. Repository notes are described as curated additions with content-derived IDs and union merge behavior.

The `forget` command accepts session, project or date selectors and offers dry-run/list and unforget paths. The inspected flow checks ambiguous session matches before destructive work; exclusions are applied during indexing, and README says forgotten transcripts stay excluded across rebuilds. This does not demonstrate erasure of source harness transcripts, backups or every derived copy.

Search intersects token postings and ranks hits using lexical BM25 with bounded signals including decision/outcome state, reuse and freshness. Result objects carry snippets, match counts, scores, tiers and lifecycle/withheld/cap metadata; the README documents project, harness, date and role filters plus optional embedding-based reranking.

Automatic hook recall can default to the working project, but MCP recall ranks that project and can include the rest of the machine; CLI search spans the store unless narrowed. Repository notes have checkout scope, while machine transcript history and local notes can be broader. These are defaults and filters rather than a tenant boundary.

Session identity, source paths, timestamps, role labels and message content preserve transcript provenance; commands, file touches and edit spans support blame/origin workflows. Promoted decisions can carry lifecycle labels and changed-workspace warnings. These features do not require claim-level citations or prove that a recorded decision is correct.

The architecture describes secret-pattern redaction before records are written into the derived index and warns that disabling it is unsafe. Repository notes are redacted on write and framed as untrusted when injected. Pattern-based detection does not establish complete secret detection.

Append-oriented records, token buckets/overlays, offsets, compression, incremental indexing, bounded result reads and warm-index hooks are source-visible efficiency measures. CLI/search/hooks and optional usage data expose operational information; README speed and index-footprint figures remain upstream claims, not measurements from this review.
The official pinned README and SECURITY.md were checked for a published contact email; neither publishes one. The security policy directs vulnerability reports through GitHub private reporting.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval and abstention — unmeasured. Search paths were inspected; no answerability or abstention cases were scored.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured. Index replacement and lifecycle labels are present; no correction or stale-value probes were run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured. Forget exclusion behavior was inspected; no post-delete probes or erasure audit was run.
Scope isolation — unmeasured. Project-first defaults and filters were inspected; no forbidden-scope probes were run.
Evidence support and citation coverage — unmeasured. Transcript and file/command lineage are source-visible; no claim-level adjudication was performed.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay — unmeasured. No timed retrieval or write-to-recall schedule was run.
Tokens and cost — unmeasured. No model/API usage or cost was measured.
Storage efficiency — unmeasured. Index format was inspected; no attributable storage size was collected.

limits.text: This bounded review inspected official README, architecture and security documents, index/search implementations, and note/forget command paths. It did not inspect every parser, plugin, policy option, embedding adapter, sync protocol or deployment; parser correctness across every supported harness is not established.
Local project defaults and filters do not establish tenant isolation, and forgetting from deja-vu does not prove removal from the source transcript, backups or all derived artifacts.

No runtime, tests or benchmark fixture were executed. This review cannot establish retrieval quality, indexing correctness under concurrent mutation, deletion completeness, deployed isolation, latency, cost or storage efficiency.

benchmark.note: No deja-vu runtime, tests or project benchmark workload was executed. Source inspection and upstream README claims are not project measurements.
